title: NIDCD calls a cry that brings comfort an early sign of communication
summary: NIDCD says an early sign of communication is a baby learning that a cry brings food, comfort, and company.
body: On its speech and language page, NIDCD says the first signs of communication occur when an infant learns that a cry will bring food, comfort, and companionship. The sentence is about the social use of a cry, not a schedule for how fast an adult must answer. The same page says the first three years are an intensive period for speech and language when the surroundings are full of sound and talk. It is a US institute description, not advice for one baby and not a diagnosis. Children vary, which that page also says.
